source.title: AOR-Bench: Do Large Audio Language Models Over-Refuse Pseudo-Harmful Queries?
source.authors: Jia-Xi Yang; Chaewan Chun; Jason Samuel Lucas; Yu-Chen Yang; Dongwon Lee

record.tranche_reason: The study derives a difference-in-means direction from refused and complied audio inputs and tests activation steering, reporting refusal-related outcomes. It does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless direction or the original all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.gate_note: Only the activation-steering results in Figure 6 directly bear on a claim version. The benchmark refusal rates, system-prompt comparisons, Chain-of-Thought results, and cited findings do not test the direction intervention. Figure 6's plotted values are not present in the supplied text, so outcomes are recorded from the paper's accompanying qualitative description.
record.test_reason: In three open-source audio language models, the study subtracts a difference-in-means direction at one layer and reports how refusal rates change (Figure 6). This is a result on V1 in a new setting (audio input, LALMs), not the original recipe. It is close to T4: the steering is a preliminary mitigation, and only qualitative outcomes are stated in the text.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors say activation steering can reduce over-refusal but may also lower true-refusal, "breaking the original safety alignment". MB-Score also declines. Preserving safety on harmful inputs remains challenging.
record.recipe_differences: The study computes a refused-minus-complied difference-in-means direction using last-token representations at a selected layer, then subtracts it during inference with α=1. It does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless direction or all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.problems: The activation-steering results are shown only in Figure 6, whose plotted values are absent from the supplied text. Only three selected open-source audio models are tested; the selected layer is not identified in the text. The study does not evaluate general capabilities, and reports a possible reduction in true-refusal alongside reduced over-refusal.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were left out; benchmark rates, system-prompt comparisons, and Chain-of-Thought results do not test the direction intervention.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; ablation at every layer and position; a harmful-minus-harmless direction; complete removal of refusal; preservation of general capabilities; layer selection and α sweeps.
The study applies a direction computed within each audio model. It does not test transfer across modalities, models or languages.

missing.what: MB-Score change under steering. The authors say it declines after intervention; it is a trade-off metric derived from TRR and ORR.
Per-model plotted TRR/ORR values before and after steering, and the identity of the selected layer

record.verdict_notes: The direction is computed from pseudo-harmful (Nr) and harmful (Nc) samples, which the paper also calls refused and complied groups. Which contrast is meant is unclear. Read the record's 'refused-minus-complied' description with caution. The authors treat the TRR drop as a cost of mitigation, but for V1 it is consistent with the direction mediating refusal generally. The study reports no capability checks, controls or uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: The direction is computed from refused versus complied samples, not harmful versus harmless instructions. The study does not test adding the direction, ablation at every layer and position, complete removal of refusal, or preservation of general capabilities.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Single-layer, last-token-derived diff-in-means subtraction (alpha=1) in MiMo-Audio-7B, Qwen2-Audio and Step-Audio-2-mini on AOR-Bench audio
labels.reason: The text states ORR falls only 'to some extent', so removal under this recipe is incomplete. But the verdict reason wrongly counts the TRR drop as a limit: lower refusal on harmful inputs is what V1 predicts. Evidence is qualitative, pooled and figure-only. 'Other abilities kept' is untested here, not a limit.

relation.reason: Its own intervention results (ORR, TRR, MB-Score under steering) bear on whether removing a refusal direction lowers refusal.

tranche.reason: New setting (audio LALMs, AOR-Bench audio) with refusal rates reported under subtraction of a difference-in-means direction (Figure 6). It is a preliminary mitigation, but it reports refusal rates, so it is not T4. It is not aimed at the mediation question, so it is not T2.

source_check.notes: All steering results are in Figure 6 with no numbers in the text, and claims are pooled across the three models. The layer is not numbered, the judge is DeepSeek-V3 (not recorded in the rows), and the prose says 'adding' while Eq. 3 subtracts. How the refused/complied groups are formed is ambiguous: the text samples pseudo-harmful Nr and harmful Nc, then calls them refused and complied groups.

statements.correction: 2606.21147: subtraction h - alpha*Delta h (alpha=1), refused-minus-complied mean at the last token of one unnumbered layer, in MiMo-Audio-7B, Qwen2-Audio and Step-Audio-2-mini. ORR falls 'to some extent', TRR 'may also' fall, MB-Score declines. Figure 6 only, pooled across models. Sign agrees with V1. Verdict limits_scope (incomplete removal), not challenges. Rows r1-r6.
statements.problem: The description of this study matches the text, but the study doesn't belong under a 'challenges' entry about a refusal-ward vector raising ASR or having an unstable sign. Subtracting the direction lowered refusal, the sign V1 predicts, and the record's verdict is limits_scope. The true-refusal claim rests on r2, r4 and r6, which aren't cited.

statements.correction: 2606.21147 tests subtraction only (Eq. 3, alpha=1, one selected layer). ORR falls 'to some extent' and TRR 'may also lead to a decrease', pooled, Figure 6 only, no numbers. Rows r1-r6. It doesn't speak to whether adding the vector raises refusal.
statements.problem: The description is right, but it cites only r1 (MiMo ORR) for a claim about three models and two measures. The study only subtracts the direction and never adds a refusal-ward vector, so it doesn't bear on the addition-sign conflict. Its TRR decrease is hedged ('may').
